# PowerPoint presentations

This skill is adapted to the MEGMEET Linux cloud workspace. Use the already configured **`/opt/office/venv/bin/python -I -B`** for Python Office work. Its existing environment supplies python-pptx, lxml, Pillow and pypdfium2; importing them with the unrelated default `python3` can fail. The enterprise profile disables LibreOffice Kit (`cli:false`). Do not probe or install its WASM/CLI packages, or reuse an old conversation's environment diagnosis. Do not install another Python environment. Verify the configured interpreter once if an operation fails, and distinguish missing files from missing packages in another interpreter. Do not change the employee's model or ask for credentials.

For explicit company/麦米/MEGMEET template requests, load `company-ppt-template` and use its supplied template/helper before following generic new-deck examples below. Do not replace the company template with an empty new presentation. User-specified alternative templates and negative requests take precedence.

Keep scripts and output files in the task workspace. The runtime and skill directory contain shared read-only resources. Match the requested slide language and the supplied presentation's design when editing it.

## Create and edit

Use `python-pptx` to inspect or modify an existing presentation. Inspect slide layouts, text runs, images, tables, and charts before editing. Change only the requested content, preserve mixed text formatting, and save to a new file unless the user requests an in-place edit. Rebuilding slides can discard unsupported animation, SmartArt, or other extension content.

For a new deck, use `python-pptx` with editable text, tables, and charts. Use local image assets rather than network-dependent image URLs. Set slide dimensions, text sizes, and chart data explicitly.

A minimal editable deck, run with the selected Python executable:

```python
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt

presentation = Presentation()
presentation.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
presentation.slide_height = Inches(7.5)
slide = presentation.slides.add_slide(presentation.slide_layouts[6])
title = slide.shapes.add_textbox(Inches(0.6), Inches(0.4), Inches(12), Inches(0.8))
run = title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].add_run()
run.text = "Quarterly report"
run.font.size = Pt(30)
data = CategoryChartData()
data.categories = ["Q1", "Q2"]
data.add_series("Revenue", [12, 18])
slide.shapes.add_chart(XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
                       Inches(0.8), Inches(1.6), Inches(11.5), Inches(4.8), data)
presentation.save("report.pptx")
```

Use `Inches` or `Cm` for positions and sizes and `Pt` for font sizes. To edit a generated title while retaining its other slides and charts:

```python
from pptx import Presentation

presentation = Presentation("report.pptx")
for shape in presentation.slides[0].shapes:
    if shape.has_text_frame and shape.text == "Quarterly report":
        shape.text_frame.paragraphs[0].runs[0].text = "Quarterly results"
presentation.save("report-edited.pptx")
```

Check that text and images fit the slide dimensions, titles form a useful sequence, and chart labels agree with source values. A native chart's embedded workbook is part of the deliverable and must contain the intended data. Library support for writing PPTX is not a rendering engine or a guarantee that every PowerPoint feature survives editing.

## Check and deliver

Run the shared checker with the selected Python executable; `<skill-directory>` is this loaded skill's resource base:

```text
<python> <skill-directory>/../scripts/check_office.py <presentation.pptx> --out <checks.json>
```

It checks ZIP/XML integrity and internal relationships and reports slide count and extracted text. Use repeated `--contains TEXT` arguments for required slide text and `--count N` for a requested slide count; `--contains` excludes chart text and speaker notes. Reopen the file to check the requested edits, chart data, and notes. Structural success does not establish text fit, alignment, readable contrast, or rendering fidelity.

Render for requested images/PDFs or an actionable layout check. Before generating images only for inspection, establish that the current model accepts images. If it does not, finish structural and content checks and state that visual layout was not inspected; do not rasterize slides the model cannot read, retry `read_image`, or choose a second model.

### Conversion and previews in this deployment

Use the existing authenticated company Office tool for Office→PDF conversion. Read `office_capabilities` once for exact operations if needed. Example:

```json
{"operation":"convert","input":"report-edited.pptx","output":"report-preview.pdf"}
```

Pass that object to `office_document`. Paths are relative to THIS session workspace, output is new, and the service retains the current session's identity and file access rules. Do not read `/run/secrets`, call service internals directly, invent attachment IDs, run a second Office server, or assume a `render_document` tool exists. `office_document` image editing accepts image inputs and is not a PDF→PNG operation. Its `INVALID_REQUEST` does not establish that OCR or all image capabilities are unavailable.

The existing Office service exposes limited PPTX editing via `edit`, with the same `.pptx` source/output format and `options.replacements` (`find`/`replace`) or `options.slides` as returned by `office_capabilities`. It also exposes `ocr` for images and PDFs. For complex layout use the configured Python library or company template helper. Do not interpret a failed request as proof that an entire operation is absent without checking the capability object and that request's documented parameters. OCR extracts text; it does not visually verify slide layout.

After successful conversion, make bounded sequential page images using the provided helper:

```text
/opt/office/venv/bin/python -I -B /opt/dsh/company-ppt-template/skills/company-ppt-template/scripts/preview_pdf.py --input report-preview.pdf --output-dir preview-v1
```

Use the current workspace as the working directory, or use confirmed absolute workspace paths. Optional `--pages 1 3 4` selects pages. The helper uses installed pypdfium2/Pillow without launching LibreOffice, creates a new directory containing PNG files and a manifest, limits page/pixel counts and reaps its single child on completion/timeout. It does not contact a network or inspect credentials.

When the current model supports images, inspect the manifest's actual PNGs using the current image-view tool. Check every page of a new deck, or all affected pages after an edit. Fix text overflow/overlap, wrong chart data, cropping and font substitutions. Reuse previews when source bytes did not change. A template's existing overflow is not an acceptable final-layout baseline. If the model cannot view images, retain the PPTX and PDF, report structural/content checks only and do not claim visual review or silently switch models.

Run conversions sequentially per task. On Cannot fork/resource exhaustion or a repeated conversion error, stop creating more processes and report the specific failed operation; do not repeatedly install, retry unchanged work or kill other conversations' tasks. Keep usable source files. Render success does not certify pixel-identical PowerPoint/Keynote layout or animation playback.

Call `present({"files":[{"path":"report-edited.pptx"}]})` with the actual final PPTX path. It exposes the current source file without copying or preserving its bytes, so keep that file in place and leave intermediate images and reports out of delivery unless requested. If `present` is unavailable, use the session's supported file delivery method.
